_comment: Calibration for the impeccable deep engine behind scripts/visual-discipline-check.py. Read by scripts/utils/impeccable_engine.py. A rule listed under a profile's `suppress` is NOT reported for artifacts resolving to that profile; every entry carries the reason it is suppressed, because a silent suppression is indistinguishable from a missing rule. Consumed by: scripts/utils/impeccable_engine.py. Last Updated: 2026-08-09.

screen.description: Surfaces read on a screen: the documentation site, dashboards, briefing HTML. The detector's own defaults were written for this case, so nothing is suppressed.

print.description: Documents laid out for A4 print and read as PDF. The detector's type floors are screen floors; a CSS pixel on an A4 page is not a screen pixel, so the floor rules say nothing true here.

suppress.tiny-text: 11px is a screen floor. At A4 render scale 9px sets a normal print size, and 821 of the 2167 findings measured on our doctypes were this rule alone.
suppress.undersized-ui-text: Same floor, same reason. 363 further findings, all on print labels that read correctly on paper.
suppress.line-length: The 65-75ch measure is a screen reading rule. Print columns are set to the page grid, not to a viewport.
suppress.cramped-padding: Detects children flush against a container edge. On a paged document the page box IS the inset, so the rule reads the margin as absent when it is the page margin.

doctype.description: The five locked corporate doctypes (letter, proposal, partnership, official, xpager) and anything rendered from them. Their layout is approved brand, and .claude/rules/corporate-docs.md puts changes to a locked template behind CEO approval, so where the detector and the template disagree the template wins.

suppress.kicker-above-heading: The section kicker ('The Landscape', 'Use Case Spotlight') is an approved element of the xPager template. The detector calls it a ban no brief earns back; a locked template is exactly the brief that does. 52 findings on the xPager family. Changing this needs CEO approval, not a detector rule.
suppress.numbered-section-labels: Numbered pillars (Pillar 01..05) carry the sequence the reader is meant to follow in the approved layout.
suppress.all-caps-body: Uppercase set at the label scale is part of the approved typographic system for doctype eyebrows and table headers.
suppress.wide-tracking: The tracked-uppercase label is the same approved element; the tracking is what makes it legible at that size.

plausibility._comment: Impeccable's parser emits physically impossible readings on some of our CSS. These are engine artifacts, not defects. They are filtered on VALUE, not by disabling the rule, so a genuine hit on the same rule still lands.

oversized-h1.reason: Measured 2856px on outputs/deliverables/.../brief.html. No h1 renders at that size; the parser is resolving something other than the computed font-size.

tight-leading.reason: Measured 0.11x and 0.03x on our doctype HTML. A line-height below 0.5 is not a tight leading, it is a misparse.

out_of_scope._comment: Impeccable is handed a directory and walks it itself, reaching files our own checker never visits. These are not our design surface.
